title: Review: retry transient SQLite failures in run_in_transaction
claimed_change:
Make ledger.tx.run_in_transaction(pool, work, attempts=3, backoff=0.05, sleep=time.sleep) retry transient SQLite failures (ledger.errors.is_transient).
- attempts is the total number of tries (positive int, else ValueError). Sleep backoff * 2**(n-1) after the n-th failed attempt, never after the last; when attempts run out, re-raise the last transient error. Non-transient errors roll back and propagate immediately without retry.
- Every attempt runs on its own connection from the pool. A connection whose attempt failed transiently must not be reused: close it so the pool creates a fresh one for the next attempt. Connections from successful or non-transient-failed attempts are rolled back as needed and returned for reuse.
- The pool must end every call with the same capacity it started with (no connection or slot is lost, on any path), including pools of size 1.
- Add tests.

ground_truth.description: On the transient-failure path the change calls conn.close() directly instead of pool.discard(conn). ConnectionPool counts live connections in _created and only discard() (or release()) gives the slot back, so every transient failure permanently consumes a slot: a size-1 pool raises PoolExhausted on the retry, and repeated retries exhaust any pool. Fix: pool.discard(conn).
